newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range, but pressure from dlr continues.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range, but pressure from dlr continues.

text.p: The ringgit was rangebound in late Asian trading and widely expected to decline further on commercial dollar demand from Malaysia and selling by Kuala Lumpur-based banks, dealers said on Thursday.
They said the ringgit had also weakened on unwinding of long positions against the yen and the Singapore dollar.
"The market was caught short in the last few days. The covering and rumours of central bank dollar-buying weakened the ringgit," said a foreign exchange dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the ringgit was expected to decline to around the 2.5080 level by Friday.
Dealers said Malaysia's Bank Negara was said to have bought dollars at around the 2.4990 level on Tuesday, which triggered a spate of ringgit selling.
However, there was profit-taking by Malaysian banks at 2.5050 and higher levels.
"There is also strong commercial demand for the dollar, which will only pick up further as the year-end nears," said a dealer with another Malaysian bank.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5057/67 a dollar against 2.5040/45 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
